question: Should stable-main closeout guarantee that its parent process exits at the deadline when Git cannot respond to any termination signal, rather than only timing out cooperative children?
rationale: The PR’s stated NFS/unresponsive-filesystem failure mode is not solved by a synchronous child-process timeout; choosing the permitted closeout failure semantics and process-isolation boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Guarantee parent exit at deadline
options.body: Rework the Git invocation behind a non-blocking, safely isolated boundary that reports timeout without waiting for an unresponsive child; add focused proof for that exact behavior.

options.title: Narrow the claim to cooperative children
options.body: Keep a synchronous timeout only if maintainers accept that it cannot bound an uninterruptible filesystem stall, and correct the PR’s user-impact and proof claims accordingly.

recommendation.title: Guarantee parent exit at deadline
recommendation.body: Rework the Git invocation behind a non-blocking, safely isolated boundary that reports timeout without waiting for an unresponsive child; add focused proof for that exact behavior.
